problems.question: Can an interacting quantum Yang–Mills theory be constructed rigorously in four dimensions?
problems.scope: Existence only; the mass gap is not claimed. Materials are with an external working group.

problems.question: How much does averaging over time limit the concentration of waves?
problems.scope: Claims a proof in all dimensions; a writeup and Lean artifacts are publicly released.

problems.question: How small can a set containing a unit line segment in every direction be?
problems.scope: Claims the all-dimensional result as a consequence of its local-smoothing proof.

problems.question: When can a Fourier transform be meaningfully restricted to a curved surface?
problems.scope: Also claimed as a consequence of the same local-smoothing result, not a separate AI discovery.

problems.question: Must solving fixed-width SAT require exponential time in the worst case?
problems.scope: A proposed refutation is under external examination. This does not settle P versus NP.

problems.question: Does every bounded low-degree polynomial on the Boolean cube have an influential variable?
problems.scope: PSI reports an AI-assisted proof with Lean artifacts, bearing on the structure needed for quantum query speedups.

problems.question: Can every problem whose solutions can be checked efficiently also be solved efficiently?
problems.scope: A refutation of ETH would not answer this question.

problems.question: Do all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line?
problems.scope: A central question about the distribution of prime numbers.

problems.question: Which geometric features of a smooth projective complex variety come from algebraic cycles?
problems.scope: The general conjecture remains unresolved despite known special cases.

problems.question: Does the behavior of an elliptic curve’s L-function determine the rank of its rational points?
Can one prove a positive energy gap above the vacuum in four-dimensional quantum Yang–Mills theory?
problems.scope: The existence claim above does not claim the mass gap required by the full Millennium Problem.

problems.question: Is approximating the ground-state energy of a local quantum system with a constant error allowance per interaction still QMA-hard?
problems.scope: The Hamiltonian formulation remains an open target; progress on related formulations does not establish it.
